task.title: Add longForm() with tests and a cited source
task.text:
Add an exported function longForm(setting) to src/greet.js. It takes a duration setting such as "2s" or "1h" and returns the long human-readable form using the ms package that the project already depends on: longForm("2s") returns "2 seconds" and longForm("1h") returns "1 hour".

Add tests for it to test/greet.test.js, keeping the existing tests. Install the dependencies and run the whole test suite, and keep going until it passes.

This project requires every new function to be documented with a cited source. Create docs/longForm.md with two or three sentences on what the function does, then a line starting with "Source:" that gives the title and URL of a web page documenting the ms package's long format option. Find that page with web_search and read the saved results before citing it. The URL must be one your search returned, not one recalled from memory.

finalText:
I added `longForm` to `src/greet.js`, wrote a test for it and added the doc page. After installing the dependencies, the full test suite passed on the first run (3 of 3).

- **`src/greet.js`:** `longForm(setting)` uses `ms` to turn the setting into milliseconds, then formats that number again with `{ long: true }`. So `longForm("2s")` returns `"2 seconds"` and `longForm("1h")` returns `"1 hour"`.
- **`test/greet.test.js`:** the two existing tests are unchanged. The new test checks both of those examples.
- **`docs/longForm.md`:** a short description of what the function does, then:
  `Source: ms/README.md at master · rauchg/ms — https://github.com/rauchg/ms/blob/master/README.md`

I found that page with a web search and read the saved results before citing it. Its "Time format written-out" section shows the `{ long: true }` option. My first search turned up nothing usable: the closest results were a different package (`msfmt`), an old commit and a type definitions package. So I ran a second search, and the README came from that one. The URL is copied from the search results, not from memory.
